name: John H. Bradley

roles.title: Pharmacist's Mate Second Class, USN, attached to 2nd Battalion, 28th Marines

summary: A Navy pharmacist's mate attached to the 28th Marines, awarded the Navy Cross on Iwo Jima for treating wounded men in the open under fire, and identified for seventy-one years as one of the six in Rosenthal's photograph. He was on Suribachi that morning and helped with the **first** flag, which is what the 2016 board concluded he is seen doing in the other photographs of the day; the man in Rosenthal's frame was Harold Schultz. Bradley was sent on the bond tour, came home to Antigo, Wisconsin, ran a funeral home and refused interviews for the rest of his life. His son's book *Flags of Our Fathers* is the reason most people know the story, and the correction landed after both of them were dead.
